I'm sorry

I made something for you, because I wanted to say it properly.

Keep scrolling

For the bickering

I'm sorry for the arguments, and for the times I let a small thing become a big one.

I'm sorry for the times I pushed when you needed space, and for the times I made a tense moment heavier than it had to be.

Your feelings matter more to me than being right, and I haven't always acted like it.

What I've noticed

When I ask questions, I know it can sound like I don't believe you. That's not what I mean, and I'm sorry it lands that way.

When it goes quiet between us, I get anxious and ask even more, and that only makes it harder for you to open up. That's on me to work on.

A lot of it comes from my own insecurity, and I don't want to put that on you. I want to work on it, and I'd love for us to build more trust together, slowly, from both sides.

I see you

I understand how exhausting it must be to feel stressed all the time, and how much more tiring it gets when we keep ending up in the same arguments.

I don't want to be one more source of that weight. I want to be a place where you can rest.

And I really want to know how to rekindle what we have: the laughing, the lightness, the way we were when we were just playing. Tell me what you need from me, and what would help us feel close again. I'm listening.

What I promise

  • To ask from curiosity, not doubt.
  • To give you room when you need it, without taking it personally.
  • To make it safe to say "I need a minute," and to trust you'll come back to me.
  • To listen to understand, not to win.
  • To come back and talk it through, every time.

What I'm asking

I don't need you to be the perfect girl in the world. I never did, and I never will.

What I need is simple: to not feel left out, to feel reassured sometimes, and for us to talk openly with each other. That's all I ask.

And I want to hear your side too. What do you need from me so you feel safe, heard and loved? I'd like us to ask each other that more often.

Us

Can we talk?

I love you, and I want to do better. Whenever you're ready.
